meta.description: Machine-readable manifest of every conformance vector collection under spec/vectors/ and the SET OF LANES REQUIRED TO CONSUME each one. This file exists to close a meta-pattern: registry consumption used to be opt-in per lane, by hardcoded filename, so a new collection was invisible to four of the five lanes by default — which is exactly how the malformed-layout vectors shipped unconsumed by Swift and Kotlin. tools/check-vector-registry.mjs (a required conformance target) fails when a vector file exists on disk but is not listed here, when a listed file is missing, when a collection is empty, when a collection's reason/failing vocabulary drifts from the declaration here, or when a required lane's declared consumer file does not reference the collection. Lanes that legitimately do not consume a collection carry an explicit exempt reason — silent omission is not expressible.
meta.no_warranty: Conformance metadata only; not production templates or advice.

lanes.js: Reference lane. tools/check-spec-vectors.mjs walks spec/vectors/ and fails closed on unrecognized or empty files (mode 'walker'); dedicated sdk-js tests are the witness where they exist.
lanes.swift: sdk-swift XCTest suite (requires DEVELOPER_DIR pointing at full Xcode).
lanes.kotlin: sdk-kotlin JUnit suite (./gradlew :core:test; JVM-only, runs in CI).

python.exempt: sdk-py has no federation/attestation layer (spec/federation.md is implemented only by sdk-js in v0.6); when the lane grows one, replace this exemption with a consumer

rust.exempt: verifier-rust has no federation/attestation layer; when the lane grows one, replace this exemption with a consumer

swift.exempt: sdk-swift has no federation/attestation layer; when the lane grows one, replace this exemption with a consumer

kotlin.exempt: sdk-kotlin has no federation/attestation layer; when the lane grows one, replace this exemption with a consumer

notes: spec/lineage.md (manifest.predecessors). Per-vector `predecessors` supplies the linkage pool (paths relative to the collection file); `expected.lineage` pins {declared, ok, verified_depth, entries:[{status, hop, reason?, identity_checked?, capsule_id?, artifact_observed_version?, artifact_error_count_min?}]}; `artifact_error_count_min` is a FLOOR on `entries[i].artifact.error_count` because that count is lane-local (per-channel error lists composed in js/py/rust, failing checks in swift/kotlin) — it pins the report-honesty invariant that an artifact reported as failing never also reports zero errors; `expected.qualifiers` is the EXACT array a lane's result must carry once `x-` vendor entries are stripped — not a lineage-scoped subset: since the verdict surface landed (spec/results.md), each pinned array lists whichever of the TEN names that fixture and host configuration genuinely produce — the base names (e.g. `signer_set_unbound`, `actor_set_unbound`, `empty_chain_not_walked`, `trust_not_evaluated`) beside the three lineage names, in the spec-defined order. All three members are ignore-if-absent so every consumer can parse collections that do not use them. Linkage is REPORT-ONLY: the ok-true-under-mismatch vectors are normative — a lane that fails the capsule on a mismatched supply is non-conforming. `predecessors-in-v06-capsule-is-inert` is equally normative in the other direction: the era gate applies to the SUBJECT capsule, not only to hops, so a lane that shape-checks the member inside a pre-lineage-era capsule rejects an artifact a v0.6 reader accepts. The frozen v0.6 predecessor fixture is a byte-identical copy of version-compat/output/known-previous-version-0.6.capsule; the generator's --check asserts the equality and never reseals it.

sdk-swift consumer notes (declared asymmetries, never silent omissions): (1) the lane is VERIFY-side for v0.7.1 — the standalone checks, the `predecessors:` pool parameter, `CapsuleVerification.lineage`, and the L3 inner/outer equality all ship; the builder conveniences (continueFrom / declarePredecessor / rewrap) stay declared fast-follows, so this lane pins rewrap output only by verifying the reference builders' fixtures. (2) `CapsuleVerification.qualifiers` carries the ten-name vocabulary of spec/results.md — the seven base names and the three lineage names, in the spec-defined order — so `expected.qualifiers` is asserted here as the exact array (x- stripped). (3) This lane's verify surface is a check list, so a fail-closed standalone problem is the `lineage` check and the REPORT-ONLY linkage diagnoses live on `lineage.entries[].errors`; `inner_ok` is asserted against the composite L3 result, which covers the outer and inner halves together.

sdk-kotlin consumer notes (declared asymmetries, never silent omissions): (1) the lane is VERIFY-side for v0.7.1 — the standalone checks, the `predecessors` verify parameter, `CapsuleVerification.lineage`, and the three lineage names on `CapsuleVerification.qualifiers` (entries 8–10 of the ten-name spec/results.md vocabulary this lane also emits) all ship; the builder conveniences (continueFrom / declarePredecessor / rewrap) stay declared fast-follows, so this lane pins rewrap output only by verifying the reference builders' fixtures. (2) sdk-kotlin core is a plain-capsule (L2) verifier, so standalone check 4 (the inner/outer JCS equality of an ENCRYPTED SUCCESSOR) has no L3 to run in: `inner-outer-mismatch` is asserted against this lane's documented plain-only refusal, which is strictly stronger than skipping it. (3) `encrypted-predecessor-unverifiable` IS run despite its requires:['encryption'] tag — its capsule is plain and only the supplied POOL artifact is encrypted, and classifying a pool artifact reads the SIGNED envelope's cipher with no decryption path — so this lane reports the same `predecessor_unverifiable`/`encrypted_predecessor` outcome as every other lane. No pool artifact class maps to `unsupported_capability` here: an encrypted supply is a FORMAT-scope limitation of v0.7.1 declarations, not a lane capability gap, and `unsupported_capability` stays unemitted in this lane. (4) This lane's verify surface is a check list, so a fail-closed standalone problem is the `lineage` check (naming the overall verdict) while the AREA boolean `lineage.ok` carries the REPORT-ONLY linkage verdict, and the linkage diagnoses live on `lineage.entries[].errors`. (5) The collection's `keys_file` names per-actor keypairs rather than an originator allowlist, and no vector here pins a trust-dependent fact, so this lane verifies with no allowlist.

spec/profiles.md. Every negative fixture is internally coherent under default rules except the declaration under test (the declaration is inside manifest_hash and the signed envelope payload), so only the profile gate can refuse it — a lane that skips the gate verifies the fixture ok=true and fails the suite. expected.profile.* pins the profile channel; expected.verdict/verdict_reason pin the normalized surface (unsupported_profile is a verifier limitation; profile_mismatch is a capsule defect mapping to verdict 'invalid'); expected.suite pins the suite-nulling rule.

Writer obligation 12 (a builder must not seal a declaration it does not implement) has no conformance fixture: every fixture here is generated by direct document construction with TEST keys. sdk-kotlin's builder is a reference builder in the sense of that obligation — it exposes no profile parameter and emits absence, so the guard is unexpressible rather than unimplemented; this note records that instead of leaving it a silent omission.

The walker additionally enforces the collection's reason categories and decrypts the decryptable_with fixtures; sdk-js/test/semantic-binding.test.js re-derives the same attacks programmatically. Vectors tagged "requires": ["encryption"] are meaningful only to lanes with an X25519/ChaCha20 path — sdk-kotlin core (plain-only L2) skips them per the collection's own notes.

Skill trust is DERIVED from the verify result, never read from the capsule (spec/trust.md 'Skill trust'). Vectors in this collection carry a per-vector `allowlist` of keypair names resolved against keys_file ([] = verify with no allowlist), because the same capsule bytes must classify differently at hosts with different trust configurations; `expected.skill_trust` pins {capsule_signed, skills:{id: tier}} exactly. tools/check-spec-vectors.mjs additionally walks the collection in the js lane.

sdk-kotlin core is a plain-capsule (L2) verifier with no encryption path: its consumer pins the two encrypted fixtures by name (clean-encrypted, tampered-blob) to the documented plain-only refusal instead of the registry outcome. The collection is still consumed in full.

spec/versioning.md. The unknown-version fixtures are internally coherent under their DECLARED version's domain strings, so only the version gate refuses them: the pinned reasons distinguish 'this verifier is too old / the era is unknown' from malformation and tampering, and expected.observed_version pins that the verify result still REPORTS the declared version as a fact even when open is refused.

spec/results.md. expected.qualifiers is an EXACT array in the spec-defined order, compared after stripping x- vendor entries from the result. Several vectors verify the same capsule bytes under different host configurations (per-vector allowlist, allowlist_literal, accept_versions) — the host-relative qualifiers are facts about THIS verification. The encrypted vector pins encrypted_outer_only as per-result: lanes with L3 decrypt the same bytes and must not find it on the inner result.

A vector's `allowlist_literal` entries reach the verifier VERBATIM, never resolved against keys_file: a MALFORMED entry is by construction one no keypair can produce. When present, the effective allowlist is the resolved `allowlist` names (empty if the vector declares none) plus the literals; the collection-level default never applies, so all five lanes compute the same set. malformed-allowlist-entry is the reason the field exists — trust_not_evaluated is defined on the EFFECTIVE (well-formed) allowlist, and that rule once diverged (sdk-js/sdk-py/verifier-rust filtered malformed entries; sdk-swift/sdk-kotlin tested the raw set and emitted no_trusted_signer on the same bytes) while every lane's own trust tests passed. In verifier-rust the vector drives the LIBRARY surface: that lane's CLI rejects a malformed --allowlist up front as a usage error.

The two capability mechanisms coexist (spec/results.md): the encrypted vector's requires:['encryption'] gates what a plain-only lane RUNS, while the same lane's runtime verdict for such a capsule — 'unsupported' with verdict_reason 'unsupported_capability' — is pinned on real encrypted fixtures by its tamper-detection consumer (sdk-kotlin: SpecRegistryTest.assertEncryptedRefused).
